requirement:
The instructions supplied under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions` tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered
page before submitting its answer. They explain how to select the tags of
excerpts used as evidence and how to pass `used: []` when none contributed.
Finishing a page records the selected inputs without fetching more source.
rationale:
The reviewed test adequately checks `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions.content`.

The test is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]`. It carries a {test} reference to the subject.

The subject has four content obligations. Each maps to an assertion on the `instructions` string that the first successful `search_text` delivery returns:

1. **Call `finish_search` for every delivered page before submitting.** The test asserts that the instructions contain "Before submitting, close every delivered search page" and "finish_search".
2. **Explain how to select tags of excerpts used as evidence.** The test asserts the phrase "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read".
3. **Explain how to pass `used: []` when none contributed.** The test asserts the phrase "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result".
4. **Finishing records the selected inputs without fetching more source.** The test asserts the phrase "without reading more source".

The test reads the string from a real tool response. That response is the first successful search, after an earlier failed search with pattern "(" that must not consume the instructions. The assertions are therefore not tautological.

Other assertions in the test support the subject but are covered by other requirements. The first `search_structure` result on a peer session carries the same instructions. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field. Those delivery rules belong to the parent `first_search.instructions` requirement.

The test checks the content by substring phrases and not by exact text. The requirement describes the content in prose and fixes no exact wording, so this is sufficient. I found no obligation in the subject text that lacks a test.

searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
